newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise, Suez decline comment on Tractebel.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise, Suez decline comment on Tractebel.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez declined comment on Thursday on a Belgian government warning that any merger between them would hurt the interests of Belgian utility Tractebel.
"I am not in a position to make a comment on the statement by the Belgian government," Lyonnaise managing director Philippe Brongniart said.
A Suez spokeswoman said she had no comment to make whatsoever.
Brongniart said that relations between Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux were very long-standing. "We have had ties for more than 25 years since Suez is our principal shareholder," he said.
On Wednesday Belgian Economics Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo said any merger between Suez and Lyonnaise would hurt the interests of Tractebel and the Belgian state.
Tractebel is a unit of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), itself a unit of Suez.
Tractebel and Lyonnaise are both active in public utilities and waste management services.
"A merger, if it were to go ahead, would affect the strategy of SGB, and thus of Tractebel and the Tractebel units, notably operating in the energy sector in Belgium and abroad," Di Rupo said.

"The envisaged merger, even if it were only a partial merger, would seriously damage Belgian interests. Several of Tractebel's business activities are identical or close to those of Lyonnaise. Thus, Tractebel...could have a conflict of interest with its parent company, in Belgium as well as abroad," he added.
